> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **9** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57574637129bebb4a6868c465be7e1b80eed1954` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8cae2ae3980972016b27ab33b3c6f59cf3197f8e`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #20661 (body; triage 5893953164; claim 5897541483; os-dev-report 5898224404), PR #20714 (body, file list, net diff against `origin/main` `5757463712` from merge-base `fa0a4b6610`), and the check-runs on the head. Read-only throughout: `git diff origin/main...refs/review/20714`, `git show origin/main:PATH`, REST reads. Governing text: ADR-0053 D-D1 and D-E3 on `origin/main`.

### ① Derived judgments

Files: `.changeset/20661-memory-analytics-lte-whole-day-first.md` (+13), `packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-analytics-20661-lte-whole-day-first.test.ts` (+165), `packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-analytics.ts` (+93 / -19). No governed surface on the file list (the `Governed Surface Queue Guard` check agrees).

1. Declared-`datetime` bare-day `$lte`, both exits — RIGHT. On `origin/main` the mingo row (`:273`) and the SQL-echo row (`:468`) asked `nextUtcCalendarDay(comparands[0])`, and `comparands` had already been through `filterComparandStorageForm` (`comparandsFor` `:1555`, called at `:886` and `:1367`), which on a `datetime` field turns `'2026-07-28'` into the instant `'2026-07-28T00:00:00.000Z'` (`core` `temporal-storage-form.ts`, `instantMs` bare-day arm). `nextUtcCalendarDay` returns null for anything but a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` string (`spec` `calendar-day.ts:95-98`), so the bound stayed inclusive at that midnight. The diff's `lteUpperBound(authored, comparand, storageForm)` asks the helper about `raw[0]` (the authored value) and converts only the widened `nextDay` through the same per-member `storageForm`: mingo `$lt` and an echo strict less-than at `'2026-07-29T00:00:00.000Z'`. That is D-E3's sentence ("runs on the bare-day STRING first; only the resulting bound is converted to the storage form") and D-D1's placement (the rewrite on the emitter, the conversion operator-blind: `filterComparandStorageForm` is untouched). It is also `find()`'s order: `memory-driver.ts:1745-1747` widens `val`, then `store(nextDay)`. One decision, rendered by both rows, so the chart and its echo cannot disagree on it.

2. Declared-`datetime` `$lte: '9999-12-31'` — RIGHT. Before: the instant `'9999-12-31T00:00:00.000Z'` went to the helper, null came back, and the bound was inclusive at that midnight, dropping the rest of the last supported day. After: `nextUtcCalendarDay('9999-12-31')` is `UNBOUNDED_ABOVE` (`calendar-day.ts:112`), so the `unbounded` arm renders `$ne: null` / `IS NOT NULL`, which is what `find()` lowers at `memory-driver.ts:1746` and what the undeclared field already answered (#20600). Same defect, same order, inside the card's scope ("whatever the day"); pinned in the new test with the day before as the bounded control.

3. Claimed-unchanged inputs — RIGHT, each derived from the code rather than from the PR's table: (a) a full timestamp string or a `Date`: the helper returns null for the authored value and for its storage form alike, so before and after both render `$lte` on the comparand in storage form; (b) an undeclared field: `coerceTemporalValue(v, undefined)` is identity (`memory-temporal.ts:51`), so `raw[0]` equals `comparands[0]` and `storageForm(nextDay)` is `nextDay` — byte-identical `$lt '2026-07-29'`; (c) a declared `date` field: the storage form of a valid bare day is that bare day, so the widened bound converts to itself — byte-identical. The new test pins (a), (b) and (c) against `find()` and against a literal id list.

4. Other cube operators — RIGHT, unchanged. At both call sites `comparands` is now `filter.values.map(storageForm)`, with `storageForm` the same closure `comparandsFor` mapped through (`extractTableName(cube.sql)`, `resolveFieldPath(cube, member)`, `driver.filterComparandStorageForm`); the map is still eager for every operator, so every conversion and any refusal it raises happen exactly as before. Only the two `lte` rows read the new `storageForm` input; the other eleven rows read `comparands` / `raw` as they did. The one added conversion is `storageForm(nextDay)` on the `before` arm, where `nextDay` is always a valid four-digit-year bare day; none of the three canonicalisers throws on that input.

5. One consequence the prose does not name, judged RIGHT: on a declared `time` field a bare-day `$lte` now lowers to `$lt '00:00:00'` where it used to lower to `$lte '00:00:00'`, because `canonicalTimeOfDay` reads a bare day as that day's midnight. A calendar day against a wall clock is a nonsense comparison either way, and after the diff it is exactly what `find()` lowers for the same input (`memory-driver.ts:1747`), which is the card's invariant. No shipped sentence claims `time` unchanged.

6. Public surface — RIGHT, none. `LteUpperBound`, `lteUpperBound`, `MongoPredicateInput.storageForm` and `SqlPredicateInput.storageForm` are module-private. `comparandsFor` to `storageFormFor` is a `private` method rename on the exported class; nothing outside the file names either (0 hits on `origin/main` and on the head), and no api-surface baseline or ADR anchor lists them. Accept-set: `MONGO_TO_CUBE_OPERATOR` is unchanged, so no operator was added or removed; `$between` is still absent and still refuses through `uncompilableFieldOperatorError` to `unsupportedFilterError` (`code INVALID_FILTER`, `status 400`, `filter-refusal.ts:61-66`).

7. Siblings, per triage — RIGHT. `dateRange` end: `origin/main` `:1005` widens `end = String(range[1])` before it builds the string and `Date` bounds, and that path converts nothing to storage form (the bounds are raw strings and `Date`s under `$or`), so it already followed D-E3; pinned against `find()` with `$gte` / `$lte`, not changed. `$between`: unreachable on this face; the refusal is pinned on both exits with the date shape, so widening the operator map later turns that pin red at the right spot.

8. Shipped doc comments — TRUE on each claim the diff makes: both rows "used to ask about `comparands[0]`, which is already in storage form" (`:273`, `:468`); `find()` "widens `val` and converts `nextDay`" (`:1745-1747`); "on an undeclared field the storage form is the authored string" (`memory-temporal.ts:51`); `9999-12-31` "has no next day" (`calendar-day.ts:106-112`); the two `{@link storageFormFor}` sites (`:157`, `:697`) follow the rename, no stale link.

9. Test — RIGHT against the pin spec: the undeclared / declared-`datetime` pair, each asserted equal to `find()` and to a literal list, plus the echo `WHERE`; one pin per sibling found (`dateRange`; the `$between` refusal envelope on both exits); the last day and the day before; the instant and `date` controls. The file name follows the package's existing `memory-NNNNN-slug.test.ts` convention.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/driver-memory` is released (`17.5.0`, not private). The diff changes the answer of an input the face already compiled and removes or renames nothing an author or consumer can name, so it is a bug fix in a released package: `patch`, never `skip-changeset`. The changeset declares `'@objectstack/driver-memory': patch` — RIGHT. `Check Changeset`: success.

Clause-②: `no` in the changeset and in the PR body — RIGHT. No accept-set widens (the input compiled before; only its rows and echo change) and none narrows (no operator, export, key or field is removed), so no arm is due.

Shipped prose, sentence by sentence against the diff and `origin/main`:
- Changeset: every sentence TRUE — the storage form of `'2026-07-28'` on a `datetime` field is `'2026-07-28T00:00:00.000Z'`; the whole-day rule does not widen an instant; `generateSql()` echoed the same narrowed bound; the last day now asks only for a value as the undeclared field already did; the "Unchanged" list (undeclared, declared `date`, full timestamp or `Date`, `dateRange` end) holds by the derivations in ①3 and ①7; `$between` stays refused `INVALID_FILTER` / 400; nothing is removed or renamed on any public surface.
- PR body (the squash message): the line citations `:273`, `:468`, `:886`, `:1367`, `:1555`, `:1005` resolve on `origin/main` to the lines named; the base `fa0a4b6610` is the merge-base and is `e4e5222b7` plus one platform-objects / plugin-audit commit; `nextUtcCalendarDay` (`spec`) and `memory-driver.ts` are untouched (file list); D-D1 does keep the conversion operator-blind and put the rewrite on the emitters; the reach grep gives 0 non-test hits against 31 test hits, and `service-analytics` `plugin.ts:245` is a comment; the four sibling-face citations resolve (`strategies/native-sql-strategy.ts:1244` widens `values[0]` then coerces `nextDay`; `strategies/objectql-strategy.ts:548` widens `bounds.$lte`; `preview-evaluator.ts:104` `lteBound` is type-blind; `driver-mongodb` `mongodb-filter.ts:1165` widens `value` then `store(nextDay)`); the two commits behind are `9b384f63ae` and `5757463712`, neither in `driver-memory`, `spec` or `core`; `eslint.config.mjs:327` says the config never enables type-aware linting. TRUE throughout. The test, gate and ablation counts are the dev's own measurements and were not re-run here; the head's check-runs are the verdict on them.
